big_picture_notes: Judges chronicles Israel's moral and spiritual decline between Joshua's death and the monarchy. The book's primary framework is a tragic, downward-spiraling cyclical formula: Sin → Oppression → Crying Out → Deliverance (by a judge) → Rest. This cycle repeats with increasing degradation, from good judges like Othniel to deeply flawed ones like Samson. The book is bracketed by a Prologue (1:1–3:6) and Epilogue (17:1–21:25). The key refrain—'In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did what was right in his own eyes'—frames the epilogue and implicitly argues for righteous monarchy. The judges themselves fail to fill the leadership vacuum, pointing forward to Samuel and David.

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Starts with 'After the death of Joshua,' marking the post-Joshua era. Ends with the angel's rebuke at Bochim and the naming of 'Weepers' (2:5), providing narrative resolution. Held together by relentless repetition of 'did not drive out' (Heb. lo' horish), the thematic key to the entire story. This section answers why the conquest was incomplete—the theological explanation follows in Story B.

scenes.scene_name: Judah Goes Up First; Bezek Defeated
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts 'after the death of Joshua.' Ends ten thousand struck at Bezek. Devices: Judah leads—the pattern of the book opens with partial obedience.

scenes.scene_name: Adoni-bezek's Thumbs and Toes; Jerusalem Burned
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the capture of Adoni-bezek. Ends Jerusalem set afire. Devices: Poetic justice—'as I have done, so God has repaid me.'
Starts Judah in the hill country. Ends Caleb's challenge. Devices: A flashback to Joshua's faith-hero.

scenes.scene_name: Othniel Wins Achsah; the Springs Granted
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts Othniel taking Debir. Ends the upper and lower springs. Devices: Introduces the first judge through a marriage.

scenes.scene_name: The Kenites; Judah and Simeon's Gains
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the Kenites settling. Ends Hebron given to Caleb. Devices: Mixed success—victories shadowed by what follows.
Starts Benjamin failing at Jerusalem. Ends the spared man founding Luz. Devices: The drumbeat of incomplete conquest begins.

scenes.scene_name: Manasseh and Ephraim Fail to Drive Them Out
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts Manasseh's unconquered towns. Ends Canaanites among Ephraim. Devices: 'They did not drive them out'—the refrain of failure.
Starts Zebulun. Ends Naphtali living among the Canaanites. Devices: The northern tribes' compromise.
Starts the Amorites confining Dan. Ends the Amorite border. Devices: The reversal—Israel pressed back, not advancing.

Starts with 'angel of the LORD came up from Gilgal.' Ends with place named 'Bochim' (Weepers). Theological capstone: Angel confronts people's sin and provides divine consequence. People's reaction gives the place its name, ending the story.

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Starts with 'When Joshua had sent the people away' (flashback to explain apostasy's origin). Ends with 'served their gods' (3:6), summarizing the ultimate sin. Held together by explicit description of cyclical formula (2:11-19)—the theological argument that governs all following stories. This is theological introduction, not narrative.

scenes.scene_name: The New Generation That Did Not Know the LORD
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with flashback to Joshua's death. Ends with 'there arose another generation after them who did not know the LORD.' Provides crucial generational hinge. 'Knowing' (Heb. yada') is relational, not intellectual.

scenes.scene_name: The Cycle of Apostasy and Judgment
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with formula: 'And the children of Israel did evil.' Ends with 'hand of the LORD was against them for harm.' First half of cyclical formula: Sin and Oppression. Language is programmatic, setting terms for all following stories.

scenes.scene_name: Judges Raised, Then the People Relapse
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts 'the LORD raised up judges.' Ends 'they returned to corrupt ways.' Devices: The cyclical pattern stated as a thesis.

scenes.scene_name: The Nations Left to Test Israel
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the LORD's anger. Ends the nations left 'to test Israel.' Devices: Divine pedagogy—failure becomes a test of fidelity.

scenes.scene_name: The Nations Left as a Test
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with 'Now these are the nations the LORD left.' Ends with 'served their gods.' Concludes prologue by stating purpose of remaining nations and result of cycle. Flows directly into first major cycle with Othniel.

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Starts with first full iteration of cyclical formula (3:7). Ends with Shamgar's brief fragment (3:31). Applies the cyclical formula twice. Othniel's brief, perfect cycle serves as baseline; Ehud's longer, more graphic cycle shows increasing complexity. Held together by the formula itself.

scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with 'And the children of Israel did evil.' Ends with 'the land had rest forty years.' Contains all formula steps: Sin, Oppression, Cry, Deliverance, Rest. Brevity and perfection serve as baseline for later flawed judges.

scenes.scene_name: Eglon Oppresses; Ehud the Left-Handed Deliverer
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts Moab's eighteen-year oppression. Ends Ehud sent with tribute. Devices: The left-handed Benjaminite—an unlikely deliverer.

scenes.scene_name: Ehud's Hidden Dagger; the Secret Message
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the concealed double-edged sword. Ends 'I have a secret message for you.' Devices: Suspense built toward the assassination.
Starts the private chamber. Ends Ehud slipping out. Devices: Dark comedy; the dagger lost in the fat king.

scenes.scene_name: The Trumpet of Ephraim; Moab Subdued
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the delay at the locked doors. Ends ten thousand Moabites slain. Devices: Israel rallied; deliverance through one bold act.

Starts with Ehud story conclusion: 'the land had rest.' Ends with 'He also saved Israel.' One-verse fragment appended to larger story. Non-Hebrew name suggests non-Israelite raised by Yahweh, highlighting God's sovereign methods.

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Starts with 'And the children of Israel again did evil' (classic cyclical formula). Ends with Song's final line and 'rest forty years' (5:31). Chapters 4-5 are literary diptych: Chapter 4 is prose narrative; Chapter 5 is poetic 'Song of Deborah.' Held together by parallel accounts of same event with key figures appearing in both.

scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the relapse after Ehud. Ends Deborah judging under her palm. Devices: A prophetess-judge—a striking introduction.

scenes.scene_name: Deborah Summons Barak; 'The Honor Will Go to a Woman'
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the call to Barak. Ends 'the LORD will deliver Sisera to a woman.' Devices: Barak's hesitancy reframes the glory.

Starts with aside about Heber the Kenite (sets up next scene). Ends with army completely routed 'by the sword.' Sisera's nine hundred chariots rendered useless. Deborah's command shows Yahweh, not Barak, as true commander.
Starts Sisera fleeing to Jael's tent. Ends the peg through his temple. Devices: Hospitality turned to ambush—the prophecy fulfilled.
Starts Barak arriving too late. Ends Jabin destroyed. Devices: The oppressor's downfall completed.

scenes.scene_name: The Song Begins: 'When the LORD Marched'
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts Deborah and Barak singing. Ends Sinai trembling. Devices: A victory hymn; theophany imagery.

scenes.scene_name: The Days of Shamgar and Jael; Deborah Arose
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the desolate roads. Ends 'the people of the LORD went down to the gates.' Devices: Before-and-after contrast—oppression to deliverance.
Starts the call to wake and sing. Ends Issachar with Barak. Devices: Roll-call of the faithful tribes.

scenes.scene_name: The Tribes Who Stayed; Zebulun Risked All
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts Reuben's hesitation. Ends Zebulun and Naphtali risking their lives. Devices: Praise and blame distributed among the tribes.
Starts the kings of Canaan. Ends the curse on Meroz. Devices: Cosmic warfare—the stars and the Kishon fight for Israel.
Starts Jael's blessing. Ends Sisera fallen at her feet. Devices: Vivid, brutal poetry celebrating the deliverance.
Starts the mother watching for her son. Ends 'so perish all your enemies.' Devices: Pathos and irony—she awaits plunder that will never come.

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Starts with 'And the children of Israel did evil' (6:1). Ends with tragic summary: 'neither showed they kindness to the house of Jerubbaal' (8:35). One of longest, most complex narratives spanning three chapters. Held together by protagonist Gideon/Jerubbaal ('He who contends with Baal'). Arc moves from fearful beginning to public triumph to tragic, idolatrous end.

scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the seven-year oppression. Ends Israel crying out. Devices: Locust-like raiders; Israel driven to dens and caves.
Starts the LORD sending a prophet. Ends 'you have not obeyed me.' Devices: Indictment before deliverance.

scenes.scene_name: 'The LORD Is with You, Mighty Warrior'
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the angel under the oak. Ends 'I will be with you.' Devices: Irony—Gideon threshing in a winepress, called a warrior.

scenes.scene_name: The Sign: Fire from the Rock
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts Gideon's request for a sign. Ends fire consuming the offering. Devices: Confirmation by miracle.
Starts Gideon's fear of death. Ends the altar Jehovah-Shalom. Devices: Terror turned to peace.

scenes.scene_name: Gideon Tears Down Baal's Altar by Night
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the command against Baal. Ends 'he did it at night.' Devices: Fearful but obedient—reform begins at home.
Starts the town's fury. Ends the name Jerubbaal. Devices: Joash's clever defense; Baal's impotence implied.

scenes.scene_name: The Spirit Comes; the Army Mustered
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the Midianite invasion. Ends the tribes summoned. Devices: 'The Spirit of the LORD clothed Gideon.'

scenes.scene_name: The Fleece and the Dew, Twice
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the first fleece test. Ends the reversed second sign. Devices: Gideon's cautious, repeated seeking of assurance.

scenes.scene_name: Too Many: the Fearful Sent Home
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the army at the spring. Ends twenty-two thousand leaving. Devices: 'Lest Israel boast'—the theology of weakness.

scenes.scene_name: The Test at the Water; 300 Lappers
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the LORD's winnowing. Ends three hundred kept. Devices: God reduces the army so the victory is unmistakably his.

scenes.scene_name: The Midianite's Dream of the Barley Loaf
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts Gideon sent down to the camp. Ends the dream interpreted. Devices: Overheard reassurance—God speaks through the enemy.

scenes.scene_name: Gideon Worships; the Trumpets and Jars
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts Gideon bowing in worship. Ends the battle signal. Devices: Faith turns to action; the unconventional weapons readied.

scenes.scene_name: The Rout: Trumpets, Jars, and the Sword
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the midnight shout. Ends Midian fleeing in confusion. Devices: 'A sword for the LORD and for Gideon'—panic does the fighting.

scenes.scene_name: Midian Pursued; Oreb and Zeeb Slain
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the Israelites summoned to pursue. Ends the two princes' heads brought to Gideon. Devices: The victory pressed to completion.
Starts Ephraim's jealous protest. Ends their anger subsiding. Devices: A soft answer—'is not the gleaning of Ephraim better?'
Starts the exhausted pursuit. Ends Gideon's threats. Devices: Fellow Israelites withhold help—internal failure.
Starts the surprise attack at Karkor. Ends the two kings captured. Devices: The pursuit completed against the odds.
Starts Gideon's return. Ends the tower of Penuel torn down. Devices: Promised retribution carried out.
Starts the questioning about Tabor. Ends the kings slain. Devices: Personal vengeance—'they were my brothers.'
Starts Israel offering him rule. Ends his request for gold earrings. Devices: 'The LORD will rule over you'—right words, fatal next step.

scenes.scene_name: The Gold Ephod Becomes a Snare
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the ephod made. Ends forty years of peace. Devices: A monument to victory becomes an idol—Gideon's tragic flaw.
Starts his seventy sons. Ends his death at a good old age. Devices: Abimelech of Shechem named—the next disaster seeded.

scenes.scene_name: Israel Forgets the LORD and Gideon
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the relapse to Baal. Ends ingratitude to Gideon's house. Devices: The cycle resumes; sets up Abimelech.

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Starts with 'Now Abimelech son of Jerubbaal' (6:31 lineage connection). Ends with 'Thus God rendered the wickedness of Abimelech... the curse of Jotham came upon them' (9:57). Self-contained, tragic narrative. Does not follow cyclical pattern. No foreign oppression, no crying out, no divine deliverance. Dark commentary on choosing human king. Held together by fulfillment of Jotham's parable and theme of bloody, internecine strife.

scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with Abimelech going to mother's relatives. Ends with making him king at oak of pillar. Details conspiracy: uses maternal connection, murders 70 half-brothers on one stone. Pure godless human politics.

scenes.scene_name: The Olive, Fig, and Vine Refuse
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts Jotham on Mount Gerizim. Ends the vine's refusal. Devices: A political fable—the worthy decline to rule.
Starts the bramble's offer. Ends 'let fire come out of the bramble.' Devices: The worthless ruler—and the threat that will consume Shechem.

scenes.scene_name: Jotham Applies the Parable and Flees
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the application. Ends Jotham fleeing to Beer. Devices: A prophetic curse spoken, then fulfilled.

scenes.scene_name: Discord Sown Between Abimelech and Shechem
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts three years of rule. Ends ambushes on the road. Devices: 'God sent an evil spirit'—the curse begins to work.
Starts Gaal winning Shechem's trust. Ends his boast against Abimelech. Devices: A rival rises amid the festival.
Starts Zebul's secret message. Ends the plan to ambush at dawn. Devices: Intrigue and counter-intrigue.

scenes.scene_name: Gaal Sees the Army; Zebul Taunts Him
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the forces in position. Ends 'go out and fight.' Devices: Zebul's mockery exposes Gaal's bluster.
Starts the battle. Ends Gaal driven out. Devices: The challenger's quick collapse.

scenes.scene_name: Shechem Destroyed and Sown with Salt
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the next day's assault. Ends salt scattered on the ruins. Devices: Total destruction—the curse advancing.
Starts the people fleeing to the temple-stronghold. Ends a thousand burned. Devices: Jotham's 'fire' literally fulfilled.

scenes.scene_name: A Millstone at Thebez; Abimelech Mortally Wounded
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the siege of Thebez. Ends his armor-bearer's stroke. Devices: A woman's millstone—ignominious end for the would-be king.
Starts the army dispersing. Ends 'the curse of Jotham came on them.' Devices: Explicit moral—God repaid the wickedness.

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Starts with 'After Abimelech... Tola arose' (10:1). Ends with 'Jephthah judged Israel six years. Then died and was buried' (12:7). Groups minor judges (Tola, Jair) as preface to major story of Jephthah. Runs through full sin-oppression-cry cycle in most intense form (10:6-18), then Jephthah's rise and tragic fall. Held together by cyclical formula and Jephthah narrative.

scenes.scene_name: The Minor Judges Tola and Jair
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with 'After Abimelech.' Ends with 'Jair died and was buried.' Brief minor judge interlude. Provides narrative bridge from Abimelech to next crisis. Wealth indicators (sons on donkeys) show move toward monarchy.
Starts the sevenfold idolatry. Ends Israel in great distress. Devices: The deepest relapse yet—a catalogue of foreign gods.

scenes.scene_name: 'Go Cry to the Gods You Chose'
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts Israel's confession. Ends God's stinging refusal. Devices: Divine sarcasm exposing their fickle worship.

scenes.scene_name: Israel Repents; the Gileadites Seek a Leader
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts putting away the foreign gods. Ends 'who will lead?' Devices: God 'could bear Israel's misery no longer'—mercy stirs.
Starts the mighty warrior, son of a prostitute. Ends gathering outlaws. Devices: The rejected son—an unlikely deliverer.
Starts the elders' approach. Ends 'will I really be your head?' Devices: Reversal—those who drove him out now need him.
Starts the negotiation. Ends the vow before the LORD. Devices: Covenant language; words and vows foreshadow the tragedy.

scenes.scene_name: Jephthah's Message to the King of Ammon
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the diplomatic query. Ends Israel's wilderness journey recalled. Devices: A reasoned case before war.

scenes.scene_name: The History: Israel Did Not Take Ammon's Land
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts Edom and Moab's refusals. Ends the conquest of Sihon. Devices: Historical argument for Israel's claim.
Starts the theological appeal. Ends the king ignoring him. Devices: 'The LORD our God is judge'—diplomacy fails, war follows.
Starts the Spirit coming on him. Ends the fatal vow. Devices: Faith marred by a needless, tragic bargain.
Starts the rout of Ammon. Ends 'you have brought me low.' Devices: Triumph turned to anguish at the door.

scenes.scene_name: The Daughter's Lament; the Yearly Custom
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts her acceptance. Ends the four-day commemoration. Devices: A grievous resolution; the daughters of Israel remember.
Starts Ephraim's complaint (again). Ends the battle. Devices: Tribal jealousy turns deadly—contrast with Gideon's diplomacy.
Starts the Jordan fords seized. Ends Jephthah's death. Devices: A dialect-test slaughter—Israel turning on itself.

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Starts with 'After him, Ibzan of Bethlehem judged' (12:8). Ends with 'He had judged Israel twenty years' and burial (16:31). Groups final three minor judges (Ibzan, Elon, Abdon) as preface to long, final judge story. Complete life cycle from miraculous birth to tragic death. Unlike other judges, doesn't 'deliver' Israel; acts as lone, chaotic agent of vengeance. Represents final degradation of judge office. Held together by Nazarite vow and repeated self-destructive interactions with Philistine women.

scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the minor judge Ibzan. Ends his death. Devices: Brief annal; thirty sons and daughters.
Starts Elon. Ends Abdon's seventy donkey-riding descendants. Devices: The minor-judge list bridging to Samson.

scenes.scene_name: The Angel Announces a Nazirite Son
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the Philistine oppression. Ends 'he will begin to deliver Israel.' Devices: A barren wife; a Nazirite from the womb.

scenes.scene_name: Manoah's Wife Reports; He Prays for a Return
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts her account to Manoah. Ends the angel returning. Devices: A father's earnest desire for guidance.
Starts Manoah's question. Ends the Nazirite rules restated. Devices: Emphasis by repetition—the vow's terms.

scenes.scene_name: The Angel Ascends in the Altar Flame
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts Manoah's offer of food. Ends the angel rising in the flame. Devices: 'His name is Wonderful'—a theophany.
Starts Manoah's fear of death. Ends the Spirit beginning to stir Samson. Devices: Birth narrative closing; the deliverer arrives.
Starts the woman at Timnah. Ends 'this was from the LORD.' Devices: Providence working through Samson's flawed desire.
Starts the lion killed barehanded. Ends honey from the carcass. Devices: The riddle's secret source seeded.
Starts the feast. Ends the companions stumped. Devices: 'Out of the eater...something to eat'—the wager set.

scenes.scene_name: The Bride Pressed; She Tells the Answer
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the threats against the bride. Ends her weeping out the secret. Devices: Manipulation and betrayal—foreshadowing Delilah.

scenes.scene_name: The Riddle Answered; Thirty Slain at Ashkelon
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts 'what is sweeter than honey?' Ends the wife given to another. Devices: Samson's rage; the cycle of revenge begins.
Starts Samson returning to her. Ends 'this time I have a right.' Devices: Insult fuels the next outburst.

scenes.scene_name: The Foxes and Firebrands; 'I Merely Repaid Them'
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the three hundred foxes. Ends Samson at the cave of Etam. Devices: Escalating, grotesque revenge.

scenes.scene_name: Judah Binds Samson to Hand Him Over
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the Philistine raid. Ends Samson bound with new ropes. Devices: His own people fear him more than they trust him.

scenes.scene_name: The Jawbone of a Donkey; a Thousand Slain
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the Spirit rushing on him. Ends 'Ramath-lehi.' Devices: The ropes melt; an improbable weapon.
Starts Samson's thirst. Ends twenty years of judging. Devices: A rare prayer; God provides.

Starts with 'Samson went to Gaza.' Ends with gates carried to Hebron. Self-contained vignette. He again visits prostitute, unchanged character. 'Escape' foreshadows his inability to escape in next scene. Gates to hilltop—superhuman strength and mockery.
Starts the Philistines' bribe. Ends the first deception exposed. Devices: The cat-and-mouse game begins.
Starts Delilah's reproach. Ends 'you have mocked me.' Devices: Repetition building toward the fatal disclosure.

scenes.scene_name: 'How Can You Say You Love Me?'; the Secret Told
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts her relentless pressing. Ends his head shaved. Devices: Worn down to death; the Nazirite vow broken.

scenes.scene_name: Strength Gone; Blinded and Bound; the Hair Grows
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts 'the LORD had left him.' Ends 'his hair began to grow.' Devices: The tragic low point—and a seed of hope.
Starts the Philistine sacrifice to Dagon. Ends the temple packed with onlookers. Devices: God's deliverer made sport—humiliation at its peak.
Starts Samson's final prayer. Ends his burial. Devices: Strength restored once more; victory in death.

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Starts with 'There was a man of the hill country of Ephraim' (17:1). Ends with contrast to 'the house of God... at Shiloh' (18:31). First of two appendixes forming book's epilogue. Self-contained narrative explaining origin of idolatrous shrine at Dan. Not part of judge cycle; case study of *religious* anarchy. Held together by refrain 'In those days there was no king in Israel' and journey of Micah's stolen idols/corrupt priest.

scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts with 'There was a man.' Ends with key refrain: 'In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did what was right in his own eyes' (17:6). Dark satire of pious apostasy. Steals from mother, she curses, he confesses, she consecrates stolen silver to make idol.

scenes.scene_name: A Wandering Levite Comes to Micah
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the Levite from Bethlehem. Ends seeking a place to stay. Devices: Rootless religion in 'the days when there was no king.'
Starts the offer of wages. Ends 'now I know the LORD will be good to me.' Devices: Privatized, transactional worship—deep irony.
Starts Dan seeking land. Ends 'your journey has the LORD's approval.' Devices: A corrupt oracle blesses a doomed venture.

scenes.scene_name: Laish Scouted: 'The Land Is Very Good'
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the spies at Laish. Ends 'God has given it into your hands.' Devices: A peaceful, defenseless people targeted.

scenes.scene_name: Six Hundred Danites at Micah's House
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the armed migration. Ends standing at the gate. Devices: Force gathering around the shrine.

scenes.scene_name: They Steal the Idols and the Priest
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the idols taken. Ends the priest gladly joining them. Devices: 'Better to be priest to a tribe'—mercenary religion.
Starts Micah's outcry. Ends 'what do you have left?' Devices: Might makes right in a lawless age.

scenes.scene_name: Laish Burned, Renamed Dan; the Idol Set Up
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the defenseless city destroyed. Ends the idol there 'all the time the house of God was at Shiloh.' Devices: Apostasy institutionalized.

stories.story_title: The Gibeah Outrage and Civil War
stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Starts with 'And it came to pass in those days, when there was no king in Israel' (19:1). Ends with 'In those days there was no king in Israel: every man did that which was right in his own eyes' (21:25)—book's final verse. Ultimate case study of anarchy when 'no king.' Single, unbroken story arc: Crime → Judgment → Consequences → 'Solution.' Details moral and political disintegration ending in brutal civil war and morally bankrupt solution. Held together by 'no king' refrain and single narrative flow.

scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts 'in those days Israel had no king.' Ends the father-in-law's welcome. Devices: The ominous frame-refrain returns.
Starts the delayed departures. Ends leaving late in the day. Devices: Hospitality stretched to a fateful delay.
Starts passing by Jebus. Ends no one taking them in. Devices: Gibeah of Benjamin—worse than the pagans, foreshadowed.

scenes.scene_name: An Old Man Takes Them In
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the old man from the fields. Ends the guests refreshed. Devices: A flicker of hospitality before horror.
Starts the wicked men surrounding the house. Ends the concubine collapsing at the door. Devices: A deliberate echo of Sodom—Israel's depth of corruption.

scenes.scene_name: The Concubine Cut into Twelve Pieces
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the Levite's cold command. Ends 'nothing like this has ever happened.' Devices: A grisly summons to national reckoning.
Starts the nation gathering 'as one man.' Ends Benjamin hearing of it. Devices: Rare unity—over an atrocity.
Starts his account. Ends 'give your verdict.' Devices: A self-serving retelling that still demands justice.
Starts the people rising as one. Ends the army united against the city. Devices: Resolve to purge the evil.

scenes.scene_name: Benjamin Refuses to Surrender the Guilty
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the demand for the wicked men. Ends the armies numbered. Devices: Tribal loyalty over justice—civil war looms.
Starts inquiring of God. Ends weeping before the LORD. Devices: Costly defeats despite a just cause—humbling Israel.
Starts the second defeat. Ends 'tomorrow I will deliver them.' Devices: Phinehas and the ark; persistence rewarded.
Starts the ambush positioned. Ends the fierce fighting. Devices: Strategy shifts the tide.
Starts the LORD striking Benjamin. Ends the feigned retreat. Devices: The trap from Joshua's Ai replayed.
Starts the column of smoke. Ends Benjamin overtaken. Devices: Panic as the city burns behind them.
Starts the thousands fallen. Ends the towns put to the sword. Devices: Near-extinction of a tribe—horror upon horror.

scenes.scene_name: The People Mourn the Lost Tribe
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the weeping at Bethel. Ends building an altar. Devices: Grief over the self-inflicted wound.

scenes.scene_name: The Oath That Created the Crisis
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Starts the oath against giving daughters. Ends 'how can we provide wives?' Devices: A rash vow compounds the disaster (cf. Jephthah).
